1	import { LocalFileGroup } from './useFileTree'
2	import { SelectionItem } from './useSelection'
3	
4	// All ancestor group keys of a group key, from outermost to the key itself
5	// — e.g. "invoices/2026/jan" -> ["invoices", "invoices/2026", "invoices/2026/jan"]
6	// — derived from the '/'-joined key scheme GroupNode/FileList use to
7	// identify groups, without needing to walk the tree.
8	function keyChain(groupKey: string): string[] {
9	  const parts = groupKey.split('/')
10	  return parts.map((_, i) => parts.slice(0, i + 1).join('/'))
11	}
12	
13	// Maps every file's path to its immediate parent group's key, or null for a
14	// root-level file with no group to inherit from.
15	function fileParentKeys(tree: LocalFileGroup): Map<string, string | null> {
16	  const result = new Map<string, string | null>()
17	  const walk = (group: LocalFileGroup, groupKey: string | null) => {
18	    for (const file of group.files) result.set(file.path, groupKey)
19	    for (const sub of group.subgroups) {
20	      walk(sub, groupKey !== null ? `${groupKey}/${sub.name}` : sub.name)
21	    }
22	  }
23	  walk(tree, null)
24	  console.log(result)
25	  return result
26	}
27	
28	// Drops any selected item that's a descendant of another selected subfolder,
29	// so a batch assignment gives only the topmost selected item in each
30	// subtree its own assignment and leaves the rest to inherit it — instead of
31	// pinning every descendant with a redundant override that could later
32	// diverge from its ancestor's.
33	export function pruneSelectionForAssignment(tree: LocalFileGroup, items: SelectionItem[]): SelectionItem[] {
34	  const selectedGroupKeys = new Set(items.filter(i => i.type === 'group').map(i => i.key))
35	  const parentKeys = fileParentKeys(tree)
36	
37	  return items.filter(item => {
38	    if (item.type === 'group') {
39	      const ancestors = keyChain(item.key).slice(0, -1)
40	      return !ancestors.some(k => selectedGroupKeys.has(k))
41	    }
42	    const parentKey = parentKeys.get(item.path) ?? null
43	    if (parentKey === null) return true
44	    return !keyChain(parentKey).some(k => selectedGroupKeys.has(k))
45	  })
46	}

content.text:
Yes, worth merging — and it's more than tidiness. In `index.tsx:72`:

```ts
setPickerTargets(pruneSelectionForAssignment(tree, selection.items))
```

`pruneSelectionForAssignment` is typed to return `SelectionItem[]`, but it's being assigned into `pickerTargets`, which is `PickerTarget[]`. That only type-checks today because the two unions happen to be structurally identical — there's already an implicit assumption baked into the code that "a selected item" and "an assignment target" are the same thing. If either type drifted independently (e.g. someone added a field to one), this call site would break in a confusing way.

I'd keep the definition in `useSelection.ts` (it's the more foundational concept — selection exists independent of the picker) and have `useDriveAssignments.ts` import `SelectionItem` and use it directly as the parameter/return type wherever it currently says `PickerTarget`, dropping the separate type alias. `GroupNode.tsx` and `FileList.tsx` would just import `SelectionItem` instead.

Want me to make that change?

18	  setFileOverride: (filePath: string, assignment: DriveAssignment) => void
19	  clearFileOverride: (filePath: string) => void
20	}

22	// Tracks Drive folder assignments made directly on a subfolder group or on
23	// an individual file (a file-level assignment overrides its group's).
24	// Resolving the *effective* assignment for a given group/file (own, else
25	// inherited from the nearest ancestor group, else none) is the caller's
26	// job, since only the caller knows the tree structure to walk.
27	export function useDriveAssignments(): DriveAssignmentsHandle {
28	  const [groupAssignments, setGroupAssignments] = useState<Map<string, DriveAssignment>>(new Map())
29	  const [fileOverrides, setFileOverrides] = useState<Map<string, DriveAssignment>>(new Map())
30	
31	  const setGroupAssignment = useCallback((groupKey: string, assignment: DriveAssignment) => {
32	    setGroupAssignments(prev => new Map(prev).set(groupKey, assignment))
33	  }, [])
34	
35	  const clearGroupAssignment = useCallback((groupKey: string) => {
36	    setGroupAssignments(prev => {
37	      const next = new Map(prev)
38	      next.delete(groupKey)
39	      return next
40	    })
41	  }, [])
42	
43	  const setFileOverride = useCallback((filePath: string, assignment: DriveAssignment) => {
44	    setFileOverrides(prev => new Map(prev).set(filePath, assignment))
45	  }, [])
46	
47	  const clearFileOverride = useCallback((filePath: string) => {
48	    setFileOverrides(prev => {
49	      const next = new Map(prev)
50	      next.delete(filePath)
51	      return next
52	    })
53	  }, [])
54	
55	  return { groupAssignments, fileOverrides, setGroupAssignment, clearGroupAssignment, setFileOverride, clearFileOverride }
56	}
57	
58	// Effective Drive assignment for every file in the tree: its own override,
59	// else the nearest ancestor group's assignment, else null. Mirrors the
60	// inheritance walk GroupNode/FileList do inline during render (same
61	// groupKey scheme: joined by '/', rooted at each top-level subgroup's own
62	// name), but usable outside a render tree — e.g. to check whether every
63	// file is ready to upload, or to build an upload job list.
64	export function resolveEffectiveAssignments(
65	  tree: LocalFileGroup,
66	  { groupAssignments, fileOverrides }: Pick<DriveAssignmentsHandle, 'groupAssignments' | 'fileOverrides'>
67	): Map<string, DriveAssignment | null> {
68	  const result = new Map<string, DriveAssignment | null>()
69	
70	  const walk = (group: LocalFileGroup, groupKey: string | null, inherited: DriveAssignment | null) => {
71	    const effective = (groupKey !== null ? groupAssignments.get(groupKey) : undefined) ?? inherited
72	    for (const file of group.files) {
73	      result.set(file.path, fileOverrides.get(file.path) ?? effective)
74	    }
75	    for (const sub of group.subgroups) {
76	      walk(sub, groupKey !== null ? `${groupKey}/${sub.name}` : sub.name, effective)
77	    }
78	  }
79	  walk(tree, null, null)
80	
81	  return result
82	}

Good idea for the pure data-shape types — less so for the hook-return types. Concretely:

- **Move**: `LocalFile`/`LocalFileGroup` (in `useFileTree.ts`, used in 8 files), `DriveAssignment` (in `useDriveAssignments.ts`, used in 6 files), and `SelectionItem` (in `useSelection.ts`, used in 5 files). These are domain data shapes referenced from all over, not really "owned" by the hook they happen to be defined in.
- **Leave alone**: `SelectionHandle`, `InclusionHandle`, `DriveAssignmentsHandle` — each is just "the shape this hook returns," used by at most a couple of consumers plus the hook itself. Moving those to `types.ts` would add a layer of indirection without reducing coupling, since you'd still need to read the hook to make sense of its handle type.

19	// Flat, ordered list of every file in the tree (a group's own files, then
20	// its subgroups' files, recursively). Shared by the upload worker (order to
21	// process files in), the upload modal's per-group rollup counts, and the
22	// "every file in this group is done" check driving the Open-in-Drive link —
23	// one traversal so they can't drift out of sync on how they handle nesting.
24	export function flattenFiles(group: LocalFileGroup): LocalFile[] {
25	  return [...group.files, ...group.subgroups.flatMap(flattenFiles)]
26	}
27	
28	export interface FileTreeHandle {
29	  root: string | null
30	  tree: LocalFileGroup | null
31	  loading: boolean
32	  error: string | null
33	  // Resolves to whether a folder was actually picked (false if the user
34	  // cancelled the dialog), so callers know when a fresh root replaced the
35	  // previous one and any per-root state (e.g. the upload queue) should reset.
36	  pickRoot: () => Promise<boolean>
37	}
38	
39	export function useFileTree(): FileTreeHandle {
40	  const [root, setRoot] = useState<string | null>(null)
41	  const [tree, setTree] = useState<LocalFileGroup | null>(null)
42	  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
43	  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
44	
45	  const pickRoot = useCallback(async () => {
46	    const folder = await PickFolder('Choose Root Folder')
47	    if (!folder) return false
48	
49	    setRoot(folder)
50	    setLoading(true)
51	    setError(null)
52	    try {
53	      setTree(await ScanLocalRoot(folder))
54	    } catch (e) {
55	      setTree(null)
56	      setError(String(e))
57	    } finally {
58	      setLoading(false)
59	    }
60	    return true
61	  }, [])
62	
63	  return { root, tree, loading, error, pickRoot }
64	}

1	import { useState, useCallback, useEffect } from 'react'
2	import { LocalFileGroup } from './useFileTree'
3	
4	export type SelectionItem = { type: 'file'; path: string } | { type: 'group'; key: string }
5	
6	function itemKey(item: SelectionItem): string {
7	  return item.type === 'file' ? `file:${item.path}` : `group:${item.key}`
8	}
9	
10	export interface SelectionHandle {
11	  size: number
12	  items: SelectionItem[]
13	  isSelected: (item: SelectionItem) => boolean
14	  // Plain click: replaces the selection with just this item.
15	  replace: (item: SelectionItem) => void
16	  // Cmd/Ctrl-click: adds or removes this item from the existing selection.
17	  toggle: (item: SelectionItem) => void
18	}
19	
20	// The shared multi-selection of files and subfolders driving both row
21	// highlighting and (Step 3e) batch Drive folder assignment — a single
22	// selection concept rather than a separate preview-only highlight.
23	export function useSelection(tree: LocalFileGroup | null): SelectionHandle {
24	  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<Map<string, SelectionItem>>(new Map())
25	
26	  // Resets on every fresh scan, like inclusion — a new root's rows aren't
27	  // the ones that were selected under the old one.
28	  useEffect(() => {
29	    setSelected(new Map())
30	  }, [tree])
31	
32	  const isSelected = useCallback((item: SelectionItem) => selected.has(itemKey(item)), [selected])
33	
34	  const replace = useCallback((item: SelectionItem) => {
35	    setSelected(new Map([[itemKey(item), item]]))
36	  }, [])
37	
38	  const toggle = useCallback((item: SelectionItem) => {
39	    setSelected(prev => {
40	      const key = itemKey(item)
41	      const next = new Map(prev)
42	      if (next.has(key)) next.delete(key); else next.set(key, item)
43	      return next
44	    })
45	  }, [])
46	
47	  return { size: selected.size, items: Array.from(selected.values()), isSelected, replace, toggle }
48	}

content.text:
I'd split into two subfolders based on role, and leave the rest at the root:

- **`hooks/`** — `useFileTree`, `useSelection`, `useInclusion`, `useDriveAssignments` (each + its test). These are the stateful building blocks the tree is built from.
- **`components/`** — `GroupNode`, `FileList`, `DriveAssignmentField`, `DriveFolderPickerModal` (+ test), `ResizableLeftPanel`, `ThumbnailPanel`, `UploadModal`, each with its `.module.css`. These are presentational, wired together by `index.tsx`.
- **Stay at root**: `index.tsx` (+ test/css) as the orchestrator, `types.ts` as the shared vocabulary both subfolders import, and `pruneSelection.ts`/`uploadQueue.ts` (+ tests) — pure logic modules, not hooks or components, small enough (2 files each) that a third subfolder for them would be more ceremony than payoff.

Main tradeoff: this is a new pattern for this codebase — `SplitMode` and `MergeMode` are flat (9 and 5 files) and have never needed subfolders, so you'd be introducing a convention rather than following one. It's justified here purely by `DriveUploadMode`'s size (31 files), not by any existing precedent to match.

+  const expanded = !collapsedGroups.has(groupKey)
+  const own = assignments.groupAssignments.get(groupKey) ?? null
+  const effective = own ?? inheritedAssignment
+  const inclusionState = inclusion.getGroupState(group)
+  const selected = selection.isSelected({ type: 'group', key: groupKey })
+
+  // Cmd/Ctrl-click toggles this group into/out of the shared selection. A
+  // plain click replaces the selection with just this group, and — only as
+  // a convenience when the selection held zero or one item beforehand —
+  // also toggles expand/collapse, so building a multi-selection doesn't pop
+  // groups open/closed as a side effect once it's under way.
+  const onNameClick = (e: React.MouseEvent) => {

+    if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) {
+      selection.toggle(item)
+    } else {
+      const hadZeroOrOne = selection.size <= 1
+      selection.replace(item)
+      if (hadZeroOrOne) onToggle(groupKey)
+    }
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <Box>

+          indeterminate={inclusionState === 'indeterminate'}
+          disabled={locked}

+          aria-expanded={expanded}
+          aria-label={expanded ? `Collapse ${group.name}` : `Expand ${group.name}`}
+          className={styles.chevronButton}
+        >
+          <Text size="xs" c="dimmed" className={styles.chevron}>{expanded ? '▼' : '▶'}</Text>
+        </button>

+          onClick={onNameClick}
+          className={styles.nameButton}
+        >

+        </button>

+          label={group.name}

+          isOwn={own !== null}
+          locked={locked}
+          onPick={() => onPick({ type: 'group', key: groupKey })}
+          onClear={() => assignments.clearGroupAssignment(groupKey)}
+          onOpen={() => effective && OpenDriveFolder(effective.driveFolderId).catch(handlePromiseRejection('Opening Drive folder failed'))}

+                  inclusion={inclusion}
+                  selection={selection}
+                  locked={locked}
+                  onPick={onPick}
+                  onPreviewFile={onPreviewFile}
+                />
+              ))}
+            </Stack>
+          )}
+        </Box>
+      )}
+    </Box>
+  )
+}

+import { useState, useCallback } from 'react'
+import { PickFolder, ScanLocalRoot } from '../../../../wailsjs/go/main/App'
+import { LocalFile, LocalFileGroup } from '../types'
+
+// Flat, ordered list of every file in the tree (a group's own files, then
+// its subgroups' files, recursively). Shared by the upload worker (order to
+// process files in), the upload modal's per-group rollup counts, and the
+// "every file in this group is done" check driving the Open-in-Drive link —
+// one traversal so they can't drift out of sync on how they handle nesting.
+export function flattenFiles(group: LocalFileGroup): LocalFile[] {
+  return [...group.files, ...group.subgroups.flatMap(flattenFiles)]
+}
+
+export interface FileTreeHandle {
+  root: string | null
+  tree: LocalFileGroup | null
+  loading: boolean
+  error: string | null
+  // Resolves to whether a folder was actually picked (false if the user
+  // cancelled the dialog), so callers know when a fresh root replaced the
+  // previous one and any per-root state (e.g. the upload queue) should reset.
+  pickRoot: () => Promise<boolean>
+}
+
+export function useFileTree(): FileTreeHandle {
+  const [root, setRoot] = useState<string | null>(null)
+  const [tree, setTree] = useState<LocalFileGroup | null>(null)
+  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
+  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
+
+  const pickRoot = useCallback(async () => {
+    const folder = await PickFolder('Choose Root Folder')
+    if (!folder) return false
+
+    setRoot(folder)
+    setLoading(true)
+    setError(null)
+    try {
+      setTree(await ScanLocalRoot(folder))
+    } catch (e) {
+      setTree(null)
+      setError(String(e))
+    } finally {
+      setLoading(false)
+    }
+    return true
+  }, [])
+
+  return { root, tree, loading, error, pickRoot }
+}

content.text:
Looking at it, the state you already extracted into hooks (`useFileTree`, `useSelection`, `useInclusion`, `useDriveAssignments`) covers only part of `index.tsx`'s state. Three more self-contained clusters remain inline and would fit the same pattern:

1. **Preview state** — `previewedFile`, `previewedPage`, `handlePreviewFile`, and the page-cache-eviction effect (lines 32–42). Fully self-contained, would become `usePreview()`.
2. **Upload flow** — `uploadModalOpen`, `started`, `allFiles`, `selectedFiles`, `effectiveAssignments`, `readyToUpload`, `handleUploadAll`, plus the upload-related half of `handlePickRoot` (lines 75–99, 100–107). This is the biggest cluster and the one most tangled with the render logic right now.
3. **Picker orchestration** — `pickerTargets`, `handlePicked`, `handleBatchAssign` (lines 62–73), which ties `selection`, `assignments`, and `pruneSelectionForAssignment` together into one flow.

Smaller things worth a look:
- `onPick={target => setPickerTargets([target])}` is duplicated verbatim on `GroupNode` and `FileList` (lines 174, 185) — one named callback would remove the repetition.
- `collapsedGroups`/`toggleGroup` (lines 46–53) is a candidate for the same hook treatment but is small enough (6 lines) that it's a judgment call, not a clear win.

Net effect of doing 1–3: `index.tsx` would shrink to mostly JSX wiring, consistent with the hooks/components split you just did for the rest of the folder.

1	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
2	import { CancelUpload, UploadFile } from '../../../wailsjs/go/main/App'
3	import { handlePromiseRejection } from '../../lib/globalErrorHandler'
4	
5	export type UploadStatus =
6	  /** Enqueued, waiting for the worker to reach it. */
7	  | 'queued'
8	  /** Was queued, then reverted here by cancelRemaining/cancelAll before the
9	   * worker reached it — never actually attempted. resumePaused re-queues
10	   * these in bulk. */
11	  | 'paused'
12	  /** The worker is currently awaiting UploadFile for it. */
13	  | 'uploading'
14	  /** Terminal: UploadFile resolved. */
15	  | 'done'
16	  /** Terminal: UploadFile rejected; .error holds the message. Retry re-queues it. */
17	  | 'error'
18	  /** Terminal: aborted mid-upload via cancel/cancelAll. Retry re-queues it. */
19	  | 'cancelled'
20	
21	export interface UploadJob {
22	  path: string
23	  folderId: string
24	  name: string
25	}
26	
27	export interface UploadEntry extends UploadJob {
28	  status: UploadStatus
29	  error?: string
30	}
31	
32	// Per-file upload status, driven by a sequential (concurrency = 1) worker.
33	// A module-level singleton (like ../../lib/pageCache) rather than a hook:
34	// there is only ever one upload run in flight for the app, so the queue's
35	// lifetime doesn't need to be tied to any one component instance. Callers
36	// resolve each file's destination folder/name up front and pass in an
37	// ordered list of jobs — this module only knows how to run them one at a
38	// time and track status, not about the file tree or Drive assignments.
39	const filesByPath = new Map<string, UploadEntry>()
40	let pendingPaths: string[] = []
41	const listeners = new Set<() => void>()
42	let running = false
43	let cancelled = false
44	
45	// Paths whose in-flight upload was cancelled. runQueue checks this once the
46	// awaited UploadFile call settles (success or failure) and, if present,
47	// leaves the status as 'cancelled' instead of overwriting it with
48	// 'done'/'error' — the request may have raced ahead of the abort signal, but
49	// the user's intent to cancel wins either way.
50	const cancelledInFlight = new Set<string>()
51	
52	function notify() {
53	  for (const fn of listeners) fn()
54	}
55	
56	export function subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void {
57	  listeners.add(fn)
58	  return () => listeners.delete(fn)
59	}
60	
61	export function useUploadQueueRender() {
62	  const [, setTick] = useState(0)
63	  useEffect(() => subscribe(() => setTick(t => t + 1)), [])
64	}
65	
66	export function getStatus(path: string): UploadEntry | undefined {
67	  return filesByPath.get(path)
68	}
69	
70	// True once none of the given files are still queued or uploading — i.e.
71	// each has either reached a terminal state (done/error) or was never
72	// started. Callers use this to know when it's safe to let the upload
73	// modal close.
74	export function hasSettled(paths: string[]): boolean {
75	  return !paths.some(path => {
76	    const status = filesByPath.get(path)?.status
77	    return status === 'queued' || status === 'uploading'
78	  })
79	}
80	
81	// True if any of the given files are paused — i.e. there's a cancelled batch
82	// the modal can offer to resume.
83	export function hasPaused(paths: string[]): boolean {
84	  return paths.some(path => filesByPath.get(path)?.status === 'paused')
85	}
86	
87	function updateStatus(path: string, status: UploadStatus, error?: string) {
88	  const existing = filesByPath.get(path)!
89	  filesByPath.set(path, { ...existing, status, error })
90	  notify()
91	}
92	
93	async function runQueue() {
94	  if (running) return
95	  running = true
96	  while (!cancelled && pendingPaths.length > 0) {
97	    const path = pendingPaths.shift()!
98	    const job = filesByPath.get(path)!
99	    updateStatus(path, 'uploading')
100	    try {
101	      await UploadFile(job.path, job.folderId, job.name)
102	      if (!cancelledInFlight.delete(path)) updateStatus(path, 'done')
103	    } catch (e) {
104	      if (!cancelledInFlight.delete(path)) updateStatus(path, 'error', String(e))
105	    }
106	  }
107	  running = false
108	}
109	
110	function enqueue(newJobs: UploadJob[]) {
111	  if (newJobs.length === 0) return
112	  cancelled = false
113	  for (const job of newJobs) {
114	    filesByPath.set(job.path, { ...job, status: 'queued', error: undefined })
115	    pendingPaths.push(job.path)
116	  }
117	  notify()
118	  void runQueue()
119	}
120	
121	export function start(newJobs: UploadJob[]): void {
122	  enqueue(newJobs)
123	}
124	
125	export function retry(job: UploadJob): void {
126	  enqueue([job])
127	}
128	
129	// Stops starting new files; does not abort an in-flight request. Files
130	// still waiting their turn are marked paused since they were never attempted.
131	export function cancelRemaining(): void {
132	  cancelled = true
133	  for (const path of pendingPaths) updateStatus(path, 'paused')
134	  pendingPaths = []
135	}
136	
137	// Aborts the file currently uploading. A no-op for any other status —
138	// queued files are handled by cancelRemaining, and done/error/cancelled are
139	// already settled. Marks the file 'cancelled' immediately rather than
140	// waiting on the CancelUpload round-trip or on however UploadFile's promise
141	// ends up settling.
142	export function cancel(path: string): void {
143	  if (filesByPath.get(path)?.status !== 'uploading') return
144	  cancelledInFlight.add(path)
145	  updateStatus(path, 'cancelled')
146	  CancelUpload(path).catch(handlePromiseRejection('Canceling upload failed'))
147	}
148	
149	// The modal's single Cancel button: aborts whatever is currently uploading
150	// and pauses everything still queued. Concurrency is 1, so at most one entry
151	// can be 'uploading' at a time.
152	export function cancelAll(): void {
153	  cancelRemaining()
154	  for (const path of filesByPath.keys()) cancel(path)
155	}
156	
157	// Re-queues every paused file among the given paths — i.e. resumes a batch
158	// left over from cancelAll. The file that was actually mid-upload when
159	// cancelled is left alone; it's 'cancelled', not 'paused', and already has
160	// its own per-row Retry button.
161	export function resumePaused(paths: string[]): void {
162	  const jobs = paths
163	    .map(path => filesByPath.get(path))
164	    .filter((entry): entry is UploadEntry => entry?.status === 'paused')
165	  enqueue(jobs)
166	}
167	
168	export function reset(): void {
169	  if (!hasSettled(Array.from(filesByPath.keys()))) {
170	    // Callers must only invoke this once hasSettled() is true for all files;
171	    // otherwise a request from the discarded run could still be in flight and
172	    // would resurface after this call.
173	    throw new Error('reset() called while an upload is still in flight')
174	  }
175	  cancelled = false
176	  running = false
177	  cancelledInFlight.clear()
178	  filesByPath.clear()
179	  pendingPaths = []
180	  notify()
181	}

content.text:
I'd keep it as separate props, unlike `GroupNode`/`FileList` which do take whole handles (`assignments`, `inclusion`, `selection`). Those are components that actively participate in tree-wide concepts; `ThumbnailPanel` is a generic "show this PDF's pages, tell me which one's selected" widget that doesn't know about "preview" as a concept — passing the whole `PreviewHandle` would tie it to `LocalFile` and to `usePreview` specifically, for no real benefit since it only needs two scalars out of `preview.file` (`path`, `pageCount`) plus `page`/`setPage`.

Main tradeoff: you'd trade 4 props for 1 at the call site in `index.tsx`, at the cost of `ThumbnailPanel` no longer being reusable/testable independent of that specific hook.
